data.title: Subversive ETFs Launches XXSP and XXQQ to Own the Market Without Elon Musk
data.description:
Subversive ETFs Launches XXSP and XXQQ to Own the Market Without Elon Musk

New “Redacted” ETFs offer broad market exposure without companies founded, controlled or led by Elon Musk

Subversive ETFs today launched the Subversive S&P 500 Redacted ETF (CBOE: XXSP) and the Subversive Growth 100 Redacted ETF (CBOE: XXQQ), two actively managed funds that deliver broad exposure to the S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100, respectively, while excluding equity securities of companies founded, controlled or led by Elon Musk.

Musk's companies have grown large enough that most broad market investors already carry meaningful exposure to him personally, whether they intended to or not. Few individuals carry as much weight across major U.S. indices, and his political activity and public volatility introduce a form of founder concentration that portfolios answering to clients, boards or their own convictions may want to weigh. XXSP and XXQQ give investors a straightforward way to opt out while maintaining broad market exposure, including by redirecting future contributions and dividends without selling existing holdings.

Subversive ETFs believes an index fund may be sold as the neutral choice, but a handful of names can ultimately decide how it behaves, with Musk being one of them. The funds were named Redacted to reflect exactly what they do. Everything else stays, while one name gets a black bar across it.

XXSP invests across the S&P 500 while excluding Tesla. XXQQ similarly provides exposure to companies in the Nasdaq-100 while excluding Tesla and Space Exploration Technologies Corp. Both funds will also screen out any other company Musk founds, controls or leads if it becomes eligible for inclusion in their respective investment universes.

XXSP and XXQQ join Subversive's lineup of the NANC and GOP ETFs, which track the reported stock trades of Democratic and Republican members of Congress. Subversive was built on the belief that everyday investors should have greater visibility into the people and forces shaping their portfolios. XXSP and XXQQ extend that approach to founder concentration, giving investors a straightforward way to remove exposure to a single influential founder without stepping away from the broader market.

Learn more at http://redacelon.com

About Subversive ETFs

Subversive is dedicated to investing in radical ideas that subvert the status quo, defy established norms, and actively disrupt their respective industries. Our commitment spans venture investing, public market investing, whistleblower financing, and ETFs, reflecting our belief in the transformative power of innovation across diverse domains.

Before investing you should carefully consider the Fund’s investment objectives, risks, charges and expenses. This and other information is available in the prospectus and summary prospectus available at www.subversiveetfs.com. Please read these carefully before investing.

Investing involves risk. Principal loss is possible.

Growth Investing Risk. Investors expect growth companies to increase their earnings at a certain rate that is generally higher than the rate expected for non-growth companies.

Exclusionary Investing Risk. The Fund excludes companies that are founded, controlled, led by or primarily associated with Elon Musk.

Foreign Securities Risk. Investments in securities or other instruments of non-U.S. companies involve certain risks not involved in domestic investments and may experience more rapid and extreme changes in value than investments in securities of U.S. companies.

Derivatives Risk. The Fund’s derivative investments have risks, including the imperfect correlation between the value of such instruments and the underlying assets or index; the loss of principal, including the potential loss of amounts greater than the initial amount invested in the derivative instrument; the possible default of the other party to the transaction; and illiquidity of the derivative investments.

Non-Diversification Risk. Because the Fund is “non-diversified,” it may invest a greater percentage of its assets in the securities of a single issuer or a smaller number of issuers than if it was a diversified fund.

For a full list of XXSP holdings, visit www.subversiveetfs.com/xxsp. For a full list of XXQQ holdings, visit www.subversiveetfs.com/xxqq. Holdings are subject to change.

NASDAQ 100 is a stock market index that tracks 100 of the largest non-financial companies listed on the NASDAQ stock exchange.

Distributed by Foreside Fund Services, LLC.

data.title: Tesla Supplier Simwon America Files for IPO — Update
data.description:
By Josh Beckerman 




  Simwon America, which provides parts for Tesla, filed for an initial public offering. 



  The company expects to sell 1.5 million shares and expects stockholders to offer 1 million, with an expected price range of $18 to $22 each. 



  The Lathrop, Calif., company's indirect parent companies MS Autotech Co., Ltd. and Myoung Shin Industry Co., Ltd. are listed in Korea. 



  Simwon America is seeking a Nasdaq Global Market listing under symbol SWA. 



  The company focuses on "Body-in-White" components. 



  In the risk factor section of its IPO filing, Simwon America notes that "we currently derive substantially all of our revenue from Tesla." For the fiscal year ended June 30, 2025, sales to Tesla accounted for about 99.5% of total revenue. 



  For the year ended June 30, 2026, revenue was down 13% to $323.9 million as "growth in the electric vehicle market moderated compared to prior periods." 



  The company has a 277,208-square-foot assembly facility and 198,183-square-foot fabrication facility in Lathrop. It plans to use some IPO proceeds to buy a company on the East Coast to support expansion and for expansion initiatives targeting the Mexican and Canadian markets. 





  Write to Josh Beckerman at josh.beckerman@wsj.com

data.title: Nectar MCP Brings Consumer and Creator Data to ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Copilot
data.description:
Nectar MCP Brings Consumer and Creator Data to ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Copilot

Nectar puts social, community, creator, customer care and insights teams on one platform. Now its answers come to the AI assistant businesses already use.

Nectar, the agentic growth operating system connecting businesses to consumers, today launched Nectar MCP, which connects a brand's Nectar data to ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Copilot. It is built on the Model Context Protocol, the open standard AI assistants use to connect to outside data.

This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261009909695/en/

Nectar puts social, community, creator, customer care and insights teams on one platform. Now its answers come to the AI assistant businesses already use.

AI assistants have become where a lot of marketing work happens. Teams have connected them to their sales numbers and their plans, but the assistants still can't see the customer: what people are asking for and complaining about on social media, and which creators they listen to. That is increasingly where buying decisions get made. Until now, getting that into a chat meant exporting a report from a dashboard and pasting it in or uploading spreadsheets, and most of the context was lost along the way.

Nectar MCP removes that step. Once it's connected, the assistant can work from the same data Nectar gathers through its official data partnerships with Meta, TikTok, Reddit, YouTube and X. This includes data such as the comments and mentions around the brand, the creators talking about the brand and the competitors it tracks, along with the analysis Nectar runs on all of it. Teams already ask Nectar's agent questions like these. Now they can ask them in the assistant they use for everything else:

  • Community: What are people saying about our launch, and how has sentiment shifted since it went live?
  • Creator: Find US beauty creators who've posted about our two biggest competitors in the last 90 days but never about us.
  • Social: Which trending TikTok sounds and formats in our category should we try this week, and what would an on-brand version look like?
  • Customer care: What are customers asking us most this month, and what creative would work well for meta ads?
  • Insights: We want to enter this product category, how are competitor products performing, where are they falling short?

"Every company is trying to give its AI the full picture of the business, and what customers say has been the missing piece," said Misbah Uraizee, co-founder and CEO of Nectar. "Social is the most honest signal a brand gets, and until now performance and consumer insights have lived in dashboards no AI could read. Now a marketer can ask how last week's launch landed and what to do next, and get one answer that connects what customers said with what they bought."

"Since 2023 we've been building the data infrastructure for social: the content, comments and creators and consumer signals around a brand, collected and organized as they happen," said Farah Uraizee, co-founder and CTO of Nectar. "MCP is how that reaches the rest of the business. We want Nectar to be for consumer conversations what Bloomberg is for market data, the source that every system and every agent checks first."

Availability
Nectar MCP is available today to Nectar customers. It works with ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Copilot, and with Cursor or any other MCP-compatible agent, including ones teams build themselves. Setup takes a few minutes and doesn't need an engineer. Each person sees only the Nectar workspaces they already have access to, and admins can switch access off at any time. To see it in action or book a demo, visit nectarsocial.com/mcp.

About Nectar
Nectar is the agentic growth operating system for brands. Its AI agents support customers, listen everywhere, discover and scale creator campaigns, sharing one intelligence that learns from every customer interaction. Founded in 2023 by former Meta leaders Misbah and Farah Uraizee, Nectar has raised $40.6 million to date. Menlo Ventures led its $30 million Series A, including through the Anthology Fund, Menlo's partnership with Anthropic, with participation from True Ventures, GV and Kinship Ventures. Customers include e.l.f. Beauty, Sweetgreen, Little Spoon and Liquid Death. Learn more at nectarsocial.com.

data.title: AI chip stocks wobble even as investors get clarity on a key OpenAI issue
data.description:
By Britney Nguyen

A new report paints OpenAI's financial picture in a more optimistic light

OpenAI, led by CEO Sam Altman, is reportedly on track for annualized revenue of $70 billion on a net basis by the end of the year, according to Bloomberg.

Even after investors got some apparent clarity on OpenAI's financial position, investors are back to being skittish about chip stocks.

OpenAI serves as an important indicator of ongoing demand for artificial-intelligence chips and therefore of the spending on AI infrastructure. As such, investors in Nvidia, Micron and other AI heavyweights pay close attention to data points surrounding the ChatGPT maker's financials.

Chip stocks sold off on Thursday after the Financial Times reported that OpenAI told investors it was approaching $50 billion in annualized revenue at the end of last month. That figure was $20 billion less than the roughly $70 billion figure OpenAI had previously projected, according to the Financial Times.

However, Bloomberg reported Friday that OpenAI is expecting annualized net revenue of $70 billion by the end of the year, mostly on strength in its enterprise business. At the end of September, the company reportedly saw annualized revenue of $50 billion. Annualized revenue is found by taking revenue from a month or another short period of time and using it to determine what a company could make in a full year.

That more upbeat view drove gains for Nvidia (NVDA), Micron (MU) and other chip stocks earlier Friday, but shares have since pulled back. Nvidia's stock was down fractionally near midday, as was Sandisk's (SNDK) and Micron's.

On the other hand, shares of Broadcom (AVGO), which is designing a custom chip with the AI startup, were moving up fractionally.

Because OpenAI is a private company, it isn't required to disclose financial performance and investors often look to make sense of nuggets from news reports. Another reason it's difficult to gauge OpenAI's financial position is that its preferred metrics may be different than Anthropic's.

OpenAI investors had reportedly tried to compare its annualized revenue with that of rival Anthropic, but because the frontier labs calculate this number differently, that led to inconsistencies, according to the Financial Times. Both the Financial Times and Bloomberg reported that while Anthropic includes the gross amount of some sales, such as those through its cloud partners, OpenAI only counts its share of revenue generated from its partnerships with cloud providers.

OpenAI didn't respond to MarketWatch's requests for comment on the reports.

While much of the market has figured out the differences between the net amount and the gross amount, "it's still an expectations issue given the media has always quoted and discussed [OpenAI's] run-rate revenue through a 'net revenue' lens," Jefferies equities trading analyst Jeffrey Favuzza said in a Friday note to clients.

Looking forward, Favuzza said the market will likely "be very excited" once at least one of the AI leaders goes public, which would offer transparency around actual financial data.

-Britney Nguyen

data.title: Sling Therapeutics Presents Data from Phase 2b/3 LIDS Clinical Trial Demonstrating Durability of Linsitinib in Thyroid Eye Disease at ASOPRS 57th Annual Fall Scientific Symposium
data.description:
Sling Therapeutics Presents Data from Phase 2b/3 LIDS Clinical Trial Demonstrating Durability of Linsitinib in Thyroid Eye Disease at ASOPRS 57th Annual Fall Scientific Symposium

Linsitinib achieved a statistically significant proptosis responder rate of 52% vs. 19% for placebo at Week 24 (p=0.010)

82% of Week 24 proptosis responders maintained their response through Week 72 (48 weeks after treatment completion), representing a highly favorable durability profile

Low incidence of IGF-1R–associated adverse events of special interest; no treatment-related hearing impairment reported

Confirmatory Phase 3 ORBIT pivotal trial currently enrolling moderate to severe active TED patients

Sling Therapeutics, Inc., a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing the first and only late-stage oral small-molecule therapy for thyroid eye disease (TED), today announced the presentation of efficacy, safety and new durability results from its Phase 2b/3 LIDS trial of linsitinib in adults with moderate to severe active TED. The data were highlighted in an oral presentation and in a poster session at the American Society of Ophthalmic Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery (ASOPRS) 57th Annual Fall Scientific Symposium.

Linsitinib is the first and only oral IGF-1R inhibitor in Phase 3 development and only small molecule therapy to significantly reduce proptosis in TED, with more convenient oral dosing compared to currently available IV and injectable IGF-1R inhibitors.

“Full LIDS results reinforce that linsitinib can deliver clinically meaningful proptosis reductions with a differentiated safety, delivery and durability profile,” said Ryan Zeidan, Ph.D., President and Chief Executive Officer of Sling Therapeutics. “Importantly, the data demonstrate that for the majority of proptosis responders in the trial, those improvements held for nearly a year after their last dose. This durability is particularly encouraging for patients, who are facing a disease that can remain active for years and often returns after treatment. With our confirmatory pivotal Phase 3 ORBIT trial now enrolling, we are focused on building the evidence to establish linsitinib as a convenient oral treatment that can deliver meaningful and durable benefit for people living with TED.”

“For physicians, Clinical Activity Scores are an important measure in determining whether TED is active and at risk of flaring. Data from LIDS indicates treatment with linsitinib resulted in sustained suppression of disease activity after treatment ended, with further improvement over the follow-up period,” said Raymond Douglas, M.D., Ph.D., board-certified aesthetic and reconstructive oculoplastic surgeon. “Furthermore, quality of life scores among linsitinib responders continued to rise after treatment ended, alongside sustained proptosis improvement and low disease activity. For patients living with a visible, often distressing disease, that continued improvement off therapy is an important benefit."

Presentation Highlights

Week 24 Efficacy & Safety

LIDS enrolled 90 adults with moderate to severe active TED, defined as onset within 12 months, proptosis ≥3 mm and Clinical Activity Scores (CAS) ≥4. Participants were randomized 1:1:1 to linsitinib 75 mg twice daily (BID), linsitinib 150 mg BID or placebo for 24 weeks. The primary endpoint was the proportion of proptosis responders at Week 24, defined as a reduction in proptosis of at least 2 mm from baseline.

  • Linsitinib 150 mg BID achieved a statistically significant proptosis responder rate of 51.7%, compared with 18.8% for placebo (p=0.010).
  • Linsitinib 75 mg BID achieved a proptosis responder rate of 38.9% (p=0.09 vs. placebo). The prespecified significance threshold for each dose was p<0.0125.
  • Most AEs were mild to moderate and reversible.
  • The most common treatment-emergent AEs in the 150 mg BID arm (>10% in any arm) were: diarrhea, headache and nausea (each 20.7%), fatigue (17.2%), ALT increase and hyperhidrosis (each 13.8%), muscle spasms and AST increase (each 10.3%).
  • Serious AEs occurred in 3.2% of placebo patients, 0% of 75 mg patients and 6.9% of 150 mg patients.
  • Among IGF-1R–associated adverse events of special interest:
    • No menstrual changes in any arm
    • No encephalopathy
    • Hyperglycemia occurred in one patient in each linsitinib arm
    • One report of hypoacusis and one report of tinnitus in the 150 mg arm were assessed as unrelated to treatment
  • Treatment discontinuations occurred in 16.7%, 20.0% and 33.3% of the placebo, 75 mg and 150 mg arms, respectively.

Long-term Follow Up & Durability

Twenty pooled linsitinib-treated patients who were proptosis responders at Week 24 entered a 48-week off-drug follow-up period. A post-hoc analysis of the durability of clinical response to linsitinib through Week 72 was assessed.

  • Response was maintained in:
    • 95% at Week 36, 48, and 60
    • 82% at Week 72
  • Mean CAS remained low throughout follow-up, improving from 1.2 at Week 24 to 0.8 at Week 72.
  • Mean overall Graves' Ophthalmopathy Quality of Life (GO-QoL) scores increased from 74.0 to 95.2 over the same period.
  • During follow-up, no treatment-related AEs, serious AEs or AEs leading to discontinuation were reported.

In September 2026, Sling announced a successful End-of-Phase 2 meeting with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and the initiation and active enrollment of its confirmatory Phase 3 ORBIT pivotal trial in patients with moderate to severe active TED.

About the Phase 2b/3 LIDS Trial

The LIDS Trial (NCT05276063) was a Phase 2b/3, randomized, double-masked, placebo-controlled trial evaluating the efficacy, safety and pharmacokinetics of oral linsitinib in adults with moderate to severe active TED. A total of 90 patients were randomized 1:1:1 to linsitinib 75 mg BID, linsitinib 150 mg BID or placebo for 24 weeks. Week 24 responders then entered a 48-week off-drug extension period to assess durability.

About Thyroid Eye Disease (TED)

Thyroid Eye Disease (TED) is a serious, progressive, and vision-threatening rare autoimmune disease that is estimated to affect more than 200,000 people in the U.S. TED often occurs in people living with Graves’ disease and hyperthyroidism and is caused by dysfunction in the IGF-1R (insulin-like growth factor 1 receptor) signaling pathway, which results in fibrous tissue growth behind the eyes. This leads to several negative symptoms that may have long-term, irreversible damage as the tissue growth pushes the eyes forward or causes the eyes and eyelids to become red and swollen. As the disease progresses, it can lead to pain, eye bulging (proptosis), and vision loss in severe cases, thus dramatically impacting a patient’s quality of life. TED predominantly affects women, and most frequently affects people with hyperthyroidism due to Graves’ disease. The current standard of care typically involves either invasive orbital surgery or a lengthy series of infusions with potential adverse events like loss of hearing, hyperglycemia, or menstrual cycle changes.

About Linsitinib

Linsitinib is a convenient oral small molecule in clinical development for thyroid eye disease (TED). Linsitinib inhibits IGF-1R (insulin-like growth factor 1 receptor) intracellularly. IGF-1R is a validated target in TED and the only target for currently approved therapies. Activation of the IGF-1R drives the inflammation, tissue expansion, and proptosis seen in TED. By blocking this signaling, linsitinib is designed to reduce these effects. Linsitinib has an established safety profile through treatment of more than 900 patients in 15 clinical trials in multiple diseases and has received Fast Track Designation from the U.S. FDA.

About Sling Therapeutics

Sling Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on the late-stage advancement of an oral small molecule therapy for the treatment of thyroid eye disease (TED). Linsitinib, the first and only oral small-molecule intracellular IGF-1R (insulin-like growth factor 1 receptor) inhibitor in Phase 3 clinical development, is designed to provide TED patients with an effective, convenient oral treatment option while reducing the treatment burden on patients, physicians and healthcare systems. For more information, visit www.slingtx.com.

Greenland Resources is a publicly listed Canadian and Greenlandic company developing Malmbjerg, a world-class Climax-type primary molybdenum deposit near tidewater in east-central Greenland. EU Says it Reached Understanding with China to Cut Back Hybrid Vehicle Exports

EU trade chief Maros Sefcovic said that the two regions reached a shared understanding in compliance with World Trade Organization rules that China would reduce its hybrid and plug-in hybrid exports.

----

Tokenized Stocks Bring 'Radical Change' to Markets, Cuomo Says

The former New York governor signed on as co-chairman of OKXICE, a joint venture between U.S. exchange powerhouse ICE and OKX that plans to tokenize stocks.

data.title: Go World Travel Magazine Wins Bronze for Best Editorial Travel Website in the 2026 SATW Foundation Lowell Thomas Travel Journalism Competition
data.description:
Go World Travel Magazine Wins Bronze for Best Editorial Travel Website in the 2026 SATW Foundation Lowell Thomas Travel Journalism Competition

Go World Travel Magazine Wins Bronze for Best Editorial Travel Website in the 2026 SATW Foundation Lowell Thomas Travel Journalism Competition

PR Newswire

ARVADA, Colo., Oct. 9, 2026

ARVADA, Colo., Oct. 9, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Go World Travel Magazine (GoWorldTravel.com) has won the Bronze award for Best Editorial Travel Website in the 2026 Lowell Thomas Travel Journalism Competition, sponsored by the Society of American Travel Writers Foundation (SATW Foundation). The awards were announced on October 6 at the SATW annual convention in Haywood County, North Carolina.

Go World Travel shares the honor with two other leading travel publications: BBC Travel won Gold and Azure Road won Silver. Go World Travel was recognized under the leadership of Managing Editor Janna Graber.

"We're thrilled and honored by this recognition," said Graber. "We believe travel connects people, and our goal is to inspire readers to explore the world with curiosity and respect. This award belongs to our talented team of editors, writers and photographers."

About the Lowell Thomas Travel Journalism Competition

Named for pioneering broadcaster, author and world traveler Lowell Thomas, the Lowell Thomas Competition is widely regarded as the premier travel journalism competition in North America. The SATW Foundation has sponsored it since 1984 and today awards more than $25,000 in prize money each year for print, digital, multimedia and broadcast work. The competition does not promote any destination or travel product, has no membership requirement for entrants, and is judged independently by journalism faculty.

This year, 26 judges at the University of Missouri School of Journalism reviewed 1,568 entries and gave 120 awards.

About Go World Travel Magazine

Go World Travel Magazine is an independent digital travel magazine for curious, culturally minded travelers. The digital magazine shares destination features, cultural stories, and practical travel advice from writers and photographers around the globe, publishing daily stories on travel in more than 90 countries. Through its coverage, Go World Travel seeks to foster cross-cultural understanding and help readers travel more meaningfully, engaging with local communities and returning home with a deeper sense of shared humanity. Learn more at GoWorldTravel.com.

About the SATW Foundation

The Society of American Travel Writers Foundation was founded in 1984 to honor outstanding work in travel journalism. It is a nonprofit 501(c)(3) organization whose mission is to support, celebrate and sustain excellence in travel journalism that serves the public. Full results are available at satwfoundation.org.

data.title: AHF Champions Girls’ Health, Rights and Futures on International Day of the Girl
data.description:
AHF Champions Girls’ Health, Rights and Futures on International Day of the Girl

On International Day of the Girl, observed annually on Oct. 11, AIDS Healthcare Foundation (AHF) is calling for greater action to ensure girls everywhere have the health, education, protection, and opportunities they need to thrive and reach their full potential.

Despite decades of progress, major barriers continue to limit girls’ opportunities. HIV continues to disproportionately affect girls in many parts of the world. In 2025, girls accounted for more than two-thirds of all new HIV infections among adolescents globally. In sub-Saharan Africa, almost six times as many adolescent girls acquired HIV as adolescent boys. Additionally, an estimated 133 million girls globally did not attend school in 2024. These disparities reinforce the need to ensure they have access to accurate sexual and reproductive health information and HIV prevention, testing, and treatment services that allow them to make informed decisions about their lives and health.

Child marriage remains another serious threat to girls’ health, education, and independence. Each year, 12 million girls are married before age 18. Child marriage also makes it difficult for girls to negotiate safer sex with their husbands, who are often older, leaving them especially vulnerable to HIV and other sexually transmitted infections, gender-based violence, and limited access to services and information.

“Every girl deserves the freedom to grow up healthy, stay in school and make her own decisions about her future. But millions of girls are still being denied those opportunities because of inequality, violence, child marriage, and barriers to health care and education,” said Loretta Wong, AHF Deputy Chief of Global Advocacy & Policy. “We must give girls the knowledge, resources, and support to protect their health, develop their potential, and lead change in their lives and communities. This includes championing policies and services that are responsive to the health needs of young people. We urge governments, communities, families, and civil society to break down these barriers that continue to hold girls back.”

AHF advances those goals through Girls Act, its global girl-led empowerment program that builds leadership, confidence, and life skills among girls and young women. Launched in 2016, AHF operates Girls Act programs in 37 countries across Africa, Asia, Europe, Latin America, and the Caribbean. The program focuses on HIV and STI prevention, supporting girls living with HIV to stay on treatment, reducing unplanned pregnancies, keeping girls in school, and strengthening advocacy, leadership, and peer support.

International Day of the Girl reminds us that empowering girls today creates healthier, stronger, and more equitable communities for generations to come.

AIDS Healthcare Foundation (AHF), the world’s largest HIV/AIDS healthcare organization, provides cutting-edge medicine and advocacy to more than 3.3 million people across 50 countries, including the U.S. and in Africa, Latin America/Caribbean, the Asia/Pacific Region, and Eastern Europe. In January 2025, AHF received the MLK, Jr. Social Justice Award, The King Center’s highest recognition for an organization leading work in the social justice arena. To learn more about AHF, visit us online at AIDShealth.org, find us on Facebook, and follow us on Instagram, Twitter, and TikTok.

data.title: Tata Motors Raises Bid for Italy's Iveco
data.description:
By Joshua Kirby 




  Tata Motors raised its offer for Iveco in light of delays due to regulatory approvals, pushing up the value of the planned takeover closer to just shy of 4 billion euros ($4.49 billion.) 



  India's Tata Motors said in a filing published Friday that it raised its offer to 14.40 euros a share, up 30 cents from the original 14.10 euros it had offered for the truck maker. The new offer gives the company an equity value of around 3.905 billion euros, according to the filing. Shares in Milan-listed Iveco closed Friday around the new offer level of 14.40 euros. 



  Iveco said last month its board unanimously supported the initial offer, and recommended shareholders accept the deal. The company said Friday it welcomed the increase in the offer price. 



  Tata Motors, an arm of conglomerate Tata Group that counts British luxury auto maker Jaguar among its assets, agreed last year to buy Iveco's commercial-vehicles business, with the completion of the transaction subject to the spinoff of Iveco's defense business. Italy's Leonardo agreed to buy that business earlier this year, paving the way for the takeover of the remaining business by Tata Motors. 



  Shareholders will vote on the transaction at a meeting scheduled for Oct. 16.
